body.content: Verification of the prime search: m = p^a * q^b where (a+1)(b+1) = 21. Factors of 21 are (21, 1) and (7, 3). So exponents are {20} or {6, 2}. Range: 2006 <= m <= 12004. For p^6 * q^2: If p=2, 64*q^2. q=5: 1600 (low), q=7: 3136 (ok), q=11: 7744 (ok), q=13: 10816 (ok), q=17: 18496 (high). If p=3, 729*q^2. q=2: 2916 (ok), q=5: 18225 (high). If p=5, 15625*q^2 (high). For p^2 * q^6: If q=2, p^2*64. p=7: 3136, p=11: 7744, p=13: 10816. These are identical values of m. If q=3, p^2*729. p=2: 2916. All values of m are {2916, 3136, 7744, 10816}.
body.why_keep_this: Confirms that swapping p and q in the p^6*q^2 form doesn't create new m values, just different prime assignments.
